claim: Alpha-beta returns the minimax value and, with good move ordering, searches about twice as deep for the same work; it is a pure speed-up, not an approximation.
agent_test: Check that any pruning rule we add in tree search keeps the answer the same as full expansion; compare nodes used at equal answer quality.

claim: Deep Blue (1997) won 3.5-2.5 by brute-force alpha-beta at about 200M positions/s with a hand-built evaluation; no learning.
agent_test: Not testable on an LLM; used as the contrast case for learned guidance.

claim: UCT (bandit rule at each node) is provably consistent and needs iterations that grow like alpha-beta's, so MCTS has no free lunch on small trees.
agent_test: Compare UCB-style branch selection against uniform sampling of thought branches at equal tokens.

claim: A learned policy/value network inside MCTS (AlphaZero, 80k positions/s) beat Stockfish (70M/s) in 100 games: 28W 72D 0L at 1 min/move; the 1000-game Science match under fairer conditions was 155W 6L 839D.
agent_test: Compare few guided expansions against many unguided ones at equal tokens.

claim: Search is worth a lot even when the net is strong: Leela 2292 (policy only) to 2858 (400 sims); AlphaZero 1777 to 2470; puzzle accuracy AZ 56.1 to 95.6.
agent_test: Run the same model with and without a branch-and-evaluate loop at equal tokens on puzzles with checkable answers.

claim: Self-play with no human data is sufficient for superhuman play (AlphaGo Zero 100-0 over AlphaGo Lee; AlphaZero; MuZero without rules).
agent_test: Only relevant as a ceiling; our agent has no training loop.

claim: Train-time and test-time compute trade off log-linearly in Hex: 10x more training lets test search drop about 15x.
agent_test: Not directly: we cannot train. Use as prior that a stronger base model needs less search; test by sweeping branch count across model sizes.

claim: Searchless distillation of a search engine into a 270M transformer reaches Lichess blitz 2895 vs humans but only 2299 vs bots, and fails off-distribution (Fischer random 1539 vs bots).
agent_test: Check whether cached/distilled answers hold on shifted problem formats. Gap search: the Fischer random drop is 2054 to 1539 Elo (515 points).

claim: An LLM used as policy, value and world model inside external MCTS adds about 300 Elo (100 sims: +68 internal Elo; 1000 sims: external 3191 vs 2923 alone), and gain is roughly logarithmic in simulations.
agent_test: Log-scale sweep of the number of search simulations on an LLM value-guided loop.

claim: LLM-written internal search (a minimax tree in one call, breadth up to 4, depth 2) raises strength modestly with tokens (about 2870 to 2930).
agent_test: Ask the agent to write a bounded tree in its own output and compare with external search at equal tokens.

claim: Tree search over LLM thoughts helps on tasks that need lookahead: Game of 24 GPT-4 CoT 4.0%, CoT best-of-100 49%, ToT b=5 74%.
agent_test: Replicate on 3 lookahead tasks vs best-of-N at equal tokens.

claim: Search quality is limited by the generator and the evaluator: GPT-4/GPT-4 74%, GPT-4 gen + GPT-3.5 eval 64%, GPT-3.5 gen + GPT-4 eval 31%, GPT-3.5 both 19%; generator matters more.
agent_test: Swap generator and evaluator strength in our loop.

claim: At equal compute the advantage of tree search over simpler baselines is often small or reverses: Snell finds lookahead/MCTS-like search under-performs best-of-N and beam search fades at large budget; TS-LLM's edge over CoT-SC with an ORM vote mostly vanishes on GSM8K.
agent_test: Always report best-of-N at equal tokens as the control. Gap search: Liu finds best-of-N best for 72B policies at all difficulty levels; Koh finds search beats re-ranking at equal compute in resettable agent tasks.

claim: Compute-optimal allocation by difficulty beats uniform best-of-N by about 4x in compute, and a small model with test-time compute can beat a 14x larger one on easy/medium but not hardest questions.
agent_test: Route search effort by estimated difficulty and compare to uniform allocation.

claim: MCTS-style methods with a learned or tested reward report large gains: RAP Blocksworld 6-step 0.42 vs CoT 0.00; LATS HumanEval GPT-4 92.7 vs 91.0 Reflexion; rStar-Math 7B MATH 58.8 to 90.0.
agent_test: Gains depend on external feedback and training; rerun with feedback ablated. Note LATS vs Reflexion gap is only 1.7 points at GPT-4.

claim: Search with real external feedback (unit tests, environment) is what makes agent tree search work; value from the LLM itself is weaker.
agent_test: Ablate real tests vs self-judged value in the search loop.

claim: Search does not remove blind spots: adversaries beat superhuman KataGo more than 97% (no search >99%); at 10M visits a cyclic adversary still won 72% over 50 games; patching did not close the hole.
agent_test: Probe our searched answers with adversarial inputs found by a separate agent. Gap search: Tseng et al. show defences fail again (92% after fine-tuning, 42% at 65,536 visits, ViT 78%); no study of LLM tree-search analogues was found.

claim: Strong engines predict human moves worse than a net trained on humans (Stockfish 33-41% vs Maia 46-52%), and extra rollouts hurt matching.
agent_test: Weak relevance; shows engine-optimal differs from human-explainable.

claim: A GPT trained only on chess text learns a linear board-state code (probe accuracy 99.6%, legal moves 99.8%) and fine-tuning on chess data lifts state tracking from about 30-53% to 93-99%.
agent_test: Test whether our agent tracks state explicitly (written board) vs implicitly.

claim: Off-the-shelf LLMs lose at games of complete information; GTBench finds them failing deterministic complete-information games but competitive in probabilistic ones.
agent_test: Only GTBench opened; the others are unopened memory items. Verify before use. Gap search: LLM Chess (Dec 2025) puts best reasoning model o3 (low) near 758 Elo vs Dragon and 71.1% of 76 models had abnormal finishes; Dynomight shows one model strong and chat models weak; Carlini's page gives no Elo. Still contested; Kaggle numbers not retrieved.

claim: Search-trace training works: Searchformer solves 93.7% of unseen Sokoban with up to 26.8% fewer search steps than A*.
agent_test: Training only; no direct scaffold test.

claim: MCTS beat alpha-beta in Go (huge branching, no good hand evaluation) but not clearly in chess until learned evaluation; the structural fit depends on branching factor and evaluation quality.
agent_test: Use tree search where branching is huge and evaluation is learnable; compare with plain sampling where a cheap checker exists. Gap search: R1 team found token-level MCTS did not scale; Browne notes trap states hurt UCT in chess.

claim: AlphaGo lost game 4 when its value estimate collapsed after a surprise move: search with a miscalibrated value fails abruptly.
agent_test: Watch for sudden drops in the agent's self-rated confidence mid-search; trigger re-planning. Gap search: LLM analogue is value exploitation (Snell easy-question beam degradation, Gao over-optimisation curve), but no measured value-vs-outcome curve over search states exists.

claim: On math with process reward models, the best test-time method depends on policy size and difficulty: best-of-N wins for easy items on small policies and for all difficulties at 72B, while beam or diverse tree search wins on hard items for 7B-32B policies.
agent_test: Default to wide sampling plus verifier for strong models; open a tree only for items that are hard for the model.

claim: In resettable interactive tasks (web agents), tree search beats trajectory re-ranking at about equal compute: GPT-4o on a VWA subset 37.0% with search (budget 20) vs about 30% for re-ranking that plateaus near 7 runs; 24.5% without search.
agent_test: Use search when the environment can be reset and gives feedback; keep depth and width small (5 and 5 gave +43% relative).

claim: Optimising harder against a learned evaluator eventually lowers true quality: beam search degrades on easy MATH items as budget grows; best-of-n gold reward follows d(alpha - beta d) in sqrt(KL).
agent_test: Cap search effort against a self-evaluator and prefer an external checker; do not escalate search depth when the first answer is already likely right.

claim: Long-chain RL reasoning does not make explicit sampling redundant: RL models gain at pass@1 but base models win at large k, and R1 itself shows AIME pass@1 79.8% vs pass@64 90.0% vs voting 86.7%.
agent_test: Keep a breadth step (several independent attempts and a selector) even on a reasoning model.

claim: Thinking models overthink easy problems and lose to non-thinking models at low complexity, win at medium complexity and collapse at high complexity; the collapse part is disputed as a token-limit and impossible-instance artefact.
agent_test: Gate extra search by estimated difficulty; log truncation before blaming reasoning.

claim: Classic MCTS with rollouts is a poor fit for LLM reasoning: it yields unfinished solutions and a poor compute-accuracy trade-off (Wu), token-level search space is exponentially larger than chess (R1), and UCT struggles with trap states (Browne). Rollout-free reward-balanced trees do better (7B + REBASE matches 34B at about 2x fewer FLOPs).
agent_test: If a tree is used, make it a shallow tree over whole thoughts with a budgeted allocation, not token-level MCTS.

claim: Selection, not generation, is the bottleneck without a verifier: coverage 82.9% to 98.44% (100 to 10,000 samples) but voting or reward-model selection only 40.50% to 41.41%; with a verifier SWE-bench Lite goes 15.9% to 56% at 250 samples. Diversity of plans helps: PlanSearch pass@200 77.0% vs 60.6% repeated sampling.
agent_test: Put effort into a trusted checker first; add plan-level diversity before depth.

claim: In an agentic harness (2025) frontier reasoning models play chess weakly: best o3 (low) about 758 Elo vs Dragon engine levels, random agent -122; 71.1% of 76 models had abnormal game finishes; 64.79% of failures were wrong actions (62.1% format/tool errors vs 37.9% illegal moves). More reasoning effort adds up to +20% win/loss.
agent_test: Hard-check legality and format before spending tokens on search.

claim: A distilled searchless model degrades under distribution shift: Elo 2054 on standard chess vs 1539 on Fischer random vs bots (515 points lower).
agent_test: Do not trust cached answers for changed task forms; re-verify or search live.

claim: Reasoning models are not a substitute for exact search or checking on long-horizon planning: o1 scores 97.8% on 600 Blocksworld problems but 23.63% on 110 larger ones (20-40 steps) and 52.8% on randomised Mystery Blocksworld, while a classical planner solves all.
agent_test: Pair LLM proposals with a symbolic checker or planner on long horizons.
